components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; width: 360px; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid rgba(190,200,201,0.2); border-radius: 24px; padding: 20px; box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.02); font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: rgba(190,200,201,0.6); } .ds-card-tile { display: flex; padding: 12px; border-radius: 16px; background: rgba(0,105,109,0.05); } .ds-card-main { flex: 1; min-width: 0; } .ds-card-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 17px; color: #161D1D; } .ds-card-meta { font-size: 13px; color: #3F4949; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-card-end { text-align: right; } .ds-card-amount { font-weight: 900; font-size: 18px; color: #161D1D; } .ds-card-badge { display: inline-block; margin-top: 6px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 8px; background: rgba(255,152,0,0.1); color: #EF6C00; font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; }

narrative.overview:
This is a whole office's paperwork, tidy and always in the owner's pocket. The system is calm and tidy: white surfaces on a barely tinted page, one deep teal for anything that acts, and quiet hairlines doing the work that shadows do elsewhere. Nothing competes with the documents and the figures, which are the reason anyone opened the app.

Controls are soft and sure-footed. Corners are generously rounded, fields are filled rather than outlined, and touch targets are sized for a thumb on a phone. Density is moderate: a list card holds a customer, a document number and an amount, and each screen stays one clear job.

The app is built on Material 3 and themed from a single teal seed, with Outfit as the only typeface. It follows the device's light or dark setting.
keyCharacteristics: One teal voice on white, with colour tints reserved for status and meaning.
Hairline borders and spacing separate surfaces; shadows barely register.
Soft, large shapes sized for thumbs.
Money is always the heaviest text on the card.
Material components, themed rather than replaced.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Gulf Teal is the only colour that signals action. Status hues describe a state and are never used for a button that isn't destructive.

rules.name: The Tint Not Fill Rule
rules.body: Coloured backgrounds are the hue at 5% to 10% opacity behind an icon or badge. Solid colour is for the primary action alone.

rules.name: The Heaviest Is Money Rule
rules.body: Amounts carry the heaviest weight (900) on the screen. Bold (700) is for titles, and nothing outranks a figure on a card.

rules.name: The Thumb First Rule
rules.body: The phone layout is the real layout. Wider screens rearrange the same content and never hold features the phone lacks.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: If two surfaces need separating, use a hairline or a gap before reaching for a shadow.

dos: Do use Gulf Teal for the one main action on a screen and let everything else stay quiet.
Do build list screens from the list card anatomy: icon tile, customer, meta line, amount, status badge.
Do build forms from form sections, capped at 1000px, and end document forms with the totals panel.
Do set money at weight 900 and pass the document's own currency to the formatter.
Do use Material components and theme roles rather than building equivalents.
Do use a darker shade of the status hue on new badges (700 or deeper), because the base green and amber on their own tint reach only about 2:1 to 2.5:1 contrast at 10px.
Do check new screens at phone width first.
donts: Don't add heavier shadows or lift to cards; separation comes from hairlines and spacing.
Don't fill large areas with status colours; they stay as 5% to 10% tints behind icons and badges.
Don't add iOS-style controls; the app follows Material on every platform it ships to.
Don't use a floating action button for anything except the screen's main creation action.
